title: Career Roadmap · Cyber Security Associate
summary: A Cyber Security Associate helps organizations protect computers, networks, applications, and information from unauthorized access, cyberattacks, and security incidents. The role combines networking fundamentals, operating systems, security monitoring, vulnerability management, access control, and incident response.

blocks.text: A Cyber Security Associate helps organizations protect computers, networks, applications, and information from unauthorized access, cyberattacks, and security incidents. The role combines networking fundamentals, operating systems, security monitoring, vulnerability management, access control, and incident response.
Depending on the employer, the role may focus on security operations centre (SOC) monitoring, network security, endpoint protection, vulnerability assessment, or general information security support.
Key responsibilities

items.text: Monitor security alerts from endpoint, network, and security monitoring systems.
Review logs to identify suspicious activity and potential threats.
Assist with investigating phishing emails, malware alerts, and unusual login attempts.
Support vulnerability scanning and remediation tracking.
Maintain user access permissions and follow identity-management procedures.
Help configure and monitor firewalls, endpoint protection, and other security controls.
Document incidents, investigations, and remediation actions.
Follow incident response procedures and escalate serious threats.
Assist with security audits, asset inventories, and compliance documentation.
Educate users about password security, phishing, and safe computing practices.

blocks.text: This roadmap assumes a three-year B.Voc programme. Adapt the sequence to the institution's actual semester structure.
Year 1
Foundation
Build computer, networking, and operating system fundamentals

items.text: Understand computer hardware, operating systems, filesystems, and processes.
Learn IP addressing, subnetting, DNS, DHCP, TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, and routing basics.
Practise Linux terminal commands, permissions, users, and processes.
Learn Windows administration basics, accounts, event logs, and system settings.
Understand common cyber threats, phishing, malware, and password attacks.
Study authentication, authorization, encryption, hashing, and multi-factor authentication.
Learn basic Python scripting for file handling and simple automation.
Set up an isolated virtual lab using virtual machines.

blocks.label: Practical milestone
blocks.text: Explain how a computer communicates over a network, interpret basic network traffic, and configure a secure practice environment.
Year 2
Security Operations
Learn defensive security and threat investigation

items.text: Study firewall rules, endpoint protection, VPNs, access controls, and network segmentation.
Learn how to collect and interpret Windows and Linux logs.
Practise basic packet analysis using Wireshark in a controlled lab.
Understand SIEM concepts, alert triage, event correlation, and escalation procedures.
Learn vulnerability assessment concepts, risk ratings, and remediation tracking.
Study incident response phases and evidence-preservation fundamentals.
Understand common web vulnerabilities and the OWASP Top 10.
Practise Python or shell scripting for repetitive defensive tasks.
Learn security documentation and incident ticketing.

blocks.label: Practical milestone
blocks.text: Investigate simulated alerts, document findings, and recommend defensive actions in an isolated lab.
Year 3
Job readiness
Build SOC readiness and an evidence-based portfolio

items.text: Practise security alert triage and incident documentation using simulated events.
Learn endpoint detection and response (EDR) concepts.
Investigate phishing samples safely without opening live malicious attachments.
Perform authorized vulnerability scans on designated lab systems.
Build a home lab with intentionally vulnerable training targets isolated from public networks.
Learn basic cloud security and identity-and-access management concepts.
Complete an internship or supervised project in IT support, networking, or security operations.
Practise incident-response scenarios and entry-level security interviews.
Maintain clear lab notes, diagrams, sanitized logs, and incident reports.

blocks.label: Practical milestone
blocks.text: Demonstrate a repeatable defensive investigation workflow and explain how to prioritize and escalate a security incident.

blocks.text: Recommended capstone project

blocks.label: Project
blocks.text: Mini Security Operations Centre (SOC) Investigation Lab.
Deliverables:

items.text: Set up an isolated virtual environment.
Generate or import benign sample security logs.
Collect and organize relevant events.
Identify simulated suspicious login or endpoint activity.
Investigate the timeline and supporting evidence.
Assign an appropriate severity and explain the reasoning.
Recommend containment and remediation steps.
Produce an incident report with evidence, limitations, and lessons learned.

blocks.text: Use only systems and datasets that you own or have explicit permission to access. Do not scan or test public systems without authorization.

rows.text: Troubleshoot common connectivity and network-security issues
Investigate logs and review security settings

Investigate simulated alerts and document findings
Follow a structured endpoint investigation process
Produce a clear incident report and escalation recommendation
Explain basic IAM, logging, and network controls
Consistently follow scope, privacy, and authorization requirements

blocks.text: Choose certifications based on the desired entry-level role and available budget. Practical lab experience should accompany certification study.

items.text: CompTIA Security+ — broad security fundamentals, subject to current exam requirements.
Cisco CCST Networking or Cybersecurity — foundational networking or security learning.
Cisco CCNA — useful for building stronger networking fundamentals.
Microsoft security learning paths — identity, endpoint, and security operations concepts.
ISC2 Certified in Cybersecurity (CC) — introductory cybersecurity knowledge; verify current eligibility and exam terms.
Fortinet training resources — firewall and network-security fundamentals.
Splunk or Microsoft Sentinel learning resources — log analysis and SIEM concepts.
Linux training — command-line and system administration skills.

blocks.text: Certification names, pricing, availability, and eligibility rules can change. Check the official provider website before enrolling.

blocks.label: Priority recommendation
blocks.text: Build networking and operating-system fundamentals first. Then choose a security fundamentals certification and a practical SIEM lab aligned with SOC or security associate roles.

blocks.label: Vulnerability Management

blocks.label: Cloud Security
blocks.text: Support secure cloud identities, networks, workloads, and logging.

blocks.text: Preserve and examine digital evidence using approved procedures.

blocks.label: Threat Intelligence
blocks.text: Research attacker behavior, indicators, and emerging threats.

blocks.label: Security Automation
blocks.text: Use scripting and workflow tools to reduce repetitive monitoring tasks.
For an entry-level candidate, SOC operations or network security is often a practical starting point because these paths build transferable technical skills.

AI-generated alerts and summaries can be inaccurate. Analysts must verify findings against actual logs and evidence before making security decisions.
By the end of the B.Voc programme, a job-ready student should aim to have:

items.text: Solid networking fundamentals, including IP addressing, DNS, ports, and common protocols.
Working familiarity with Linux and Windows.
Practical experience reviewing sample logs and investigating simulated alerts.
Familiarity with SIEM concepts and one learning or lab environment.
At least three documented defensive security projects.
A basic understanding of vulnerability assessment and remediation.
Introductory Python, Bash, or PowerShell scripting skills.
One relevant certification or structured course, if feasible.
An internship or supervised practical assignment in IT, networking, or security.
Clear investigation notes, incident reports, and a professional technical portfolio.
A strong understanding of authorization, privacy, and ethical security practice.

blocks.label: Recommended first career target
blocks.text: Cyber Security Associate or SOC Analyst – Tier 1.

blocks.label: Best initial strategy
blocks.text: Build strong networking and operating-system fundamentals, then develop practical skills in log analysis, SIEM alert triage, and incident documentation.

blocks.label: Most valuable differentiator
blocks.text: The ability to investigate an alert systematically, support conclusions with evidence, and document a clear escalation or remediation recommendation.

blocks.label: Long-term opportunity
blocks.text: Progress into security operations, network security, cloud security, vulnerability management, incident response, or security engineering.
